questions.question: A book of mass 0.2 kg falls vertically from rest from a shelf 1.5 m above the floor. Model the book as a particle falling freely under gravity. Find the time taken to reach the floor.
steps: Model: particle falling freely, so a = g = 9.8 m s^-2 downwards.
Take downwards as positive: u = 0, s = 1.5 m, a = 9.8 m s^-2.

questions.question: The book (mass 0.2 kg) falls from rest through 1.5 m in 0.6 s. Model it as a particle with a constant resistance to motion of magnitude R N. Use this model to find R.
steps: Model: weight 0.2 x 9.8 acts downwards and resistance R acts upwards.
Newton's second law (downwards positive): 0.2 x 9.8 - R = 0.2a.

questions.question: A motorbike with constant acceleration passes P, then 10 s later passes Q with speed 28 m s^-1. Given PQ = 220 m, find the acceleration.
steps: Let the speed at P be u. Constant acceleration a over t = 10 s.

questions.question: Using the motorbike with u = 16 m s^-1 and a = 1.2 m s^-2 from P, find the distance travelled during the fifth second after passing P.
steps: Distance in the fifth second = s(5) - s(4).

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upwards at t = 0 from a point A above horizontal ground and hits the ground 7 s later. It is modelled as a particle moving freely under gravity. The velocity-time graph (Figure 3) crosses t-axis at t = 2.5 s and reaches v = 0 there. Find the speed with which the ball is thrown.
steps: Model: free motion under gravity, so v = u - 9.8t taking upwards as positive.
From Figure 3 the ball is at its highest point (v = 0) at t = 2.5 s.

questions.question: The ball is thrown upwards at 24.5 m s^-1 from A and hits the ground 7 s later under free fall. Find the height of A above the ground.
steps: Take upwards as positive, with A as origin. The ground is at displacement -h at t = 7.
Use s = ut - (1/2)(9.8)t^2 with u = 24.5 and t = 7.
The ground is 68.6 m below A, so A is 68.6 m above the ground.

questions.question: A van with constant acceleration passes point A with speed u m s^-1 and 20 s later passes point B with speed 28 m s^-1. Given AB = 400 m, show that u = 12.
steps: Use s = (u + v)/2 x t with s = 400, v = 28, t = 20.

questions.question: A van travels from A (speed 12 m s^-1) to B (speed 28 m s^-1) in 20 s with AB = 400 m under constant acceleration. Find the time taken to travel from A to the midpoint of AB.
steps: The midpoint is 200 m from A, so 200 = 12t + (1/2)(0.8)t^2.
Reject the negative root; t = 11.9 s (3 s.f.).

questions.question: The van has mass 1200 kg and experiences a constant resistive force of magnitude 260 N while moving from A to B. Find the magnitude of the driving force from the engine.
steps: Acceleration from A to B is a = 0.8 m s^-2 (from part (b)).
Newton's second law along the road, taking the direction of motion as positive: F - 260 = 1200 x 0.8.

questions.question: A car is moving at a constant speed of 25 m s^-1 along a straight horizontal road. At t = 0 the car is at point A and the driver sees a road sign 48 m ahead. The car decelerates uniformly at 6 m s^-2 from A until it reaches the road sign. Use this first model to find the speed of the car as it reaches the sign.
steps: The sign is 48 m from A (given on the page): u = 25, a = -6, s = 48, v = ?

questions.question: Second model: the car decelerates at 6 m s^-2 from A (48 m from the road sign) until its speed is 13 m s^-1, then keeps this speed until it reaches the road sign. Use this model to find the time t when the car reaches the sign.
steps: Deceleration stage: v = u + at gives 13 = 25 - 6t1, so t1 = 2 s.
Distance in this stage: s = (u + v)t/2 = (25 + 13)(2)/2 = 38 m.
Distance left at constant speed = 48 - 38 = 10 m, so t2 = 10 / 13 = 0.769 s.

questions.question: Third model: the car moves at 25 m s^-1 from A (48 m from the road sign) until t = 0.2 s, then decelerates at 6 m s^-2 until its speed is 13 m s^-1, then keeps this speed until it reaches the road sign. Use this model to find the time t when the car reaches the sign.
steps: Constant speed stage: 0.2 s at 25 m s^-1 covers 25 x 0.2 = 5 m.
Deceleration stage (as in part b): 2 s and 38 m.
Distance left at 13 m s^-1 = 48 - 5 - 38 = 5 m, so time = 5 / 13 = 0.385 s.

questions.question: A vehicle moves from P to Q with constant acceleration. PQ = 6x m and QR = 5x m. At P the speed is u m s^-1 and at Q (12 s later) the speed is 2u m s^-1. Show that x = 3u.
steps: Use v = u + at over P to Q: 2u = u + 12a, so a = u/12.
Use s = (u + v)/2 x t: PQ = (u + 2u)/2 x 12 = 18u.

questions.question: At Q the acceleration changes to 1.5 m s^-2 and the vehicle passes R (QR = 5x) with speed 3u m s^-1, where x = 3u. Find the value of u.
steps: From Q to R: QR = 5x = 15u, a = 1.5, initial speed 2u, final speed 3u.
u is not zero, so u = 9 m s^-1.

questions.question: With u = 9, find the distance travelled by the vehicle during the first 14 s after passing P. P to Q takes 12 s and the acceleration after Q is 1.5 m s^-2.
steps: With u = 9: x = 27, so PQ = 6x = 162 m and QR = 5x = 135 m.
P to Q takes 12 s, so the first 14 s includes 2 s after Q.
Speed at Q is 2u = 18 m s^-1.
Distance in the next 2 s: 18 x 2 + (1/2)(1.5)(2^2) = 36 + 3 = 39 m.

questions.question: A parachutist steps from a helicopter at rest and falls freely from rest for 2.5 s before the parachute opens. Find his speed when the parachute opens.
steps: Model: free fall from rest, so v = 0 + 9.8t.

questions.question: Sketch a speed-time graph for the parachutist from when he leaves H until he hits the ground, with the parachute opening, deceleration for T s, and then constant speed V m s^-1 until he hits the ground.
questions.answer: Speed-time graph: straight line from (0, 0) to (2.5, 24.5), then straight line down to (7.5, 5), then horizontal line at 5 m s^-1 to (20, 5).
steps: Phase 1 (0 to 2.5 s): straight line from the origin, gradient 9.8, reaching 24.5 m s^-1.
Phase 2 (2.5 to 7.5 s): straight line with gradient -3.9, falling to V = 5 m s^-1 (from part (c)).
Phase 3 (7.5 to 20 s): horizontal line at 5 m s^-1 until he hits the ground.

questions.question: After the parachute opens at 24.5 m s^-1 the parachutist decelerates at 3.9 m s^-2 for T s (T < 6) until his speed is V m s^-1. He falls 73.75 m during this deceleration. Find T.
steps: Distance during deceleration: (24.5 + V)/2 x T = 73.75.
Since T < 6, T = 5 s, and then V = 24.5 - 19.5 = 5 m s^-1.

questions.question: The total time from leaving H to hitting the ground is 20 s. Find, to the nearest metre, the height of H above the ground.
steps: Free fall for 2.5 s: distance = (1/2)(9.8)(2.5^2) = 30.625 m.
Constant speed 5 m s^-1 for 20 - 2.5 - 5 = 12.5 s: distance = 62.5 m.

questions.question: A stone is projected vertically upwards with speed 20 m s^-1 from O, which is 5 m above horizontal ground. It is modelled as a particle moving freely under gravity. Find its speed when it is 2 m above the ground.
steps: Take upwards as positive with O as origin. The point 2 m above ground is 3 m below O, so s = -3.
Use v^2 = u^2 + 2as with u = 20 and a = -9.8.

questions.question: A stone is projected upwards at 20 m s^-1 from O, 5 m above the ground. Find the total time from projection until it first strikes the ground.
steps: Take upwards as positive with O as origin. The ground is at displacement -5.

questions.question: A car with constant acceleration a m s^-2 (a > 0) passes P with speed u m s^-1 at t = 0. In the next 4 s it travels 76 m, then in the following 6 s it travels a further 219 m. Find the value of u.
Using the same car (passing P at u m s^-1, travelling 76 m in the first 4 s and a further 219 m in the next 6 s), find the value of a.
steps: From the first 4 s: 76 = 4u + 8a, so u + 2a = 19.
a = 3.5 m s^-2 (check: u = 12 gives 76 m in 4 s and 295 m in 10 s).

questions.question: A car moves with constant acceleration a m s^-2 (a > 0) and passes A at t = 0 with speed u m s^-1. In the first 3 s after A it travels 20 m. In the fourth second after A it travels 10 m. It passes B with speed 20 m s^-1. Find the time taken to travel from A to B.
steps: Fourth second: distance = s(4) - s(3) = (4u + 8a) - (3u + 4.5a) = u + 3.5a = 10.
Use v = u + at with v = 20: 20 = 25/6 + (5/3)t, so t = 9.5 s.
